title: Affine source model on a K-flat module complex
statement: Let R,A,R',A' be commutative rings with the four ring maps whose spectra form a cartesian square [def-pc-base-change]. Let M be an A-module complex K-flat in the module-derived sense [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Let K on Spec A have quasi-coherent cohomology, and let L=Lg'^*K have quasi-coherent cohomology. Put P=tilde M termwise, supply e:QP≅K and invertibility of its pullback counit. For every i, there exist the natural affine direct-image cohomology presentation d, an A'-module U and A'-linear a:U→ΓH^i(L), and eU:tilde(restrict_R' U)≅H^i(Lg^*Rf_*K), satisfying the global base-change square. For every p of Spec A', there is an additive equivalence U_p≃source(r) taking localized a to r under the canonical affineDerivedCohomologyStalkIso, where r is the source-only comparison [def-pc-affine-base-change-into-pullback] for P=tilde M and e. This is the affine module calculation, with no arbitrary sheaf-complex representative.

proof.text: Reflect the cartesian Spec square to a pushout of commutative rings. Mathlib tensor-product pushout uniqueness constructs its algebra map to A' and proves that its two restrictions are the supplied ring maps. Instantiate the existing canonical base-derived tensor model m.

Use the explicit cohomology coordinates, module U and arrow a. Apply the global comparison to m to obtain d,eU and the global square. Apply the stalk comparison to that same m,U,a. Package these shared witnesses to prove the original existential and conjunction.
